title: How your body turns food into energy
examples: How does food give us energy?
Why do we need oxygen to get energy?

stages.label: Digest food
stages.note: Into sugars, fats and amino acids

explain.say: Food is fuel. Your body unlocks the chemical energy stored in it, not by burning it in a fire, but in a slow, controlled set of steps inside your cells.

draw.text: How your body turns food into energy

stages.label: Digest food
stages.note: Into sugars, fats and amino acids

explain.say: Digestion breaks food into small pieces: carbohydrates into sugars like glucose, fats into fatty acids, proteins into amino acids. These enter the blood and travel to every cell.

stages.label: Digest food
stages.note: Into sugars, fats and amino acids

explain.say: Inside cells, tiny structures called mitochondria combine the fuel with oxygen you breathed in. This is respiration, and it releases energy step by step.

stages.label: Digest food
stages.note: Into sugars, fats and amino acids

explain.say: The energy is stored in a molecule called ATP, which powers muscle contractions, nerve signals and building new tissue. The waste, carbon dioxide and water, is breathed out or reused.

stages.label: Digest food
stages.note: Into sugars, fats and amino acids

faq.a: Mitochondria are tiny structures inside your cells that use oxygen to break down fuel from food, releasing its energy and storing it in ATP. Busy cells like muscle cells have lots of them.
asks: What is the powerhouse of the cell?

faq.a: ATP, adenosine triphosphate, is a molecule that carries energy inside cells. Breaking off one of its phosphate parts releases energy for jobs like muscle contraction; respiration then rebuilds it.
asks: Tell me about ATP being made

faq.q: Why do we need oxygen to get energy?
faq.a: Oxygen is needed at the last step of respiration in the mitochondria. Without it, cells can release only a small fraction of the energy in glucose.
asks: Why do we breathe in oxygen?

faq.q: Why do we breathe out carbon dioxide?
faq.a: Carbon dioxide is a waste product of respiration. It passes from cells into the blood, travels to the lungs and is breathed out.
asks: Where does the carbon dioxide we breathe out come from?

faq.q: What happens to food energy we don't use straight away?
faq.a: The body stores it: some glucose as glycogen in the liver and muscles, and more as fat, which can be broken down for energy later.
asks: How does the body store energy?

facts: Aerobic respiration can be summarised as glucose plus oxygen gives carbon dioxide plus water, releasing energy.
The body recycles roughly its own body weight in ATP every day.

quiz.say: Where in a cell is most energy released from food?
quiz.show: Where in a cell is most energy released from food?
quiz.why: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration, making most of the cell's ATP.

wrong.1: The membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.
